newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bills rally slightly after lethargic day.
newsitem.headline: NZ bills rally slightly after lethargic day.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* NZ money market rallies slightly into close
New Zealand bill rates rallied slightly into Monday's close after an extremely lethargic session.
The 90-day bills ended down four basis points at 8.83 percent, while the December futures contract climbed five to 91.52. The March futures contract was up seven at 92.34.
"We continue to see this inverse cash market, and that is dragging the short end of the bill curve down a little but not anything significant," one money market dealer said.

"I think really before we can take these rates much lower we do need to get a much clearer vision of what the political future holds for us, and also just how the Reserve Bank is thinking. We haven't seen anything out of the bank for a while now -- it would be nice if they came out with some comments just to give us a bit of direction."
Meanwhile, bonds ended flat after rumours of further samurai issues failed to inspire the flagging market.
One bond dealer said he did not believe the country's current lack of a new government was the only factor holding the market in check.
"We saw some rather large selling late last week...I think that's put an offer into the market -- it's a bit of an overhang, a bit of a digestion problem," he said.

The nationalist New Zealand First Party holds the balance of power after October 12's inconclusive general election, and is negotiating with both the caretaker National Party and the centre-left Labour Party in the quest to form a new government.
